Team,

We need a concise, leadership-ready snapshot for next week’s QBR focused on: capacity hedging for expected burst traffic, and the immediate unit-econ levers (GPU spend, utilization, batching, KV cache). Goal is a 1‑page exec slide + appendix with numbers and tradeoffs.

Ask: can each of you reply by EOD Monday with the items below (fill the numbers you own):
- Current committed vs. on‑demand GPU capacity (slots / GPUs) — Karthik
- Trailing 30/90/180d utilization by pool (avg % and 95th) — Marissa
- YTD GPU spend and expected delta if we reserve an additional 50 GPUs for 3 months — Rishi
- Measured batching & KV cache impact: tokens/saved-per-GPU-hour and observed latency shift at p95 — Laura

Quick framing: we expect a product-driven burst window in late May (~3–4x baseline). We want a hedging plan that keeps 99th percentile latency within our SLA while minimizing incremental unit cost. Include: recommended reserved capacity, predicted unit cost delta, and two fallback plays (model fallback + regional routing).

Attachments: slot-usage.csv (current 7d slot dump).

I’ll assemble the exec slide once I have numbers.

—Alex

Quick numbers (high level) — I’ll drop a 2‑page appendix by EOD with raw tables.
- YTD GPU spend (hosted + reserved): $6.2M (through Mar). Monthly run-rate: $520k.
- Utilization (weighted across pools): trailing-30d avg = 63%, 95th = 88%; trailing-90d avg = 58%, 95th = 86%.
- Committed vs on-demand: 420 reserved GPUs active, burstable on-demand equivalent ~600 GPUs across clouds (quota-limited).

Reserve-50-GPUs scenario (3 months):
- Incremental committed cost: ~$95k/month (list price net of current discounts).
- Expected utilization benefit: reduces on-demand use by ~35% in burst window; estimated gross token-cost savings ~18% during those 3 months.
- Net unit cost: we model ~6–9% improvement on tokens/$.

Batching & KV cache note:
- Measured with current traffic: moving from our conservative batch window (10ms) to 25ms increased effective tokens/GPU-hour by ~22% for gen workloads; p95 latency increased ~40–70ms depending on model.
- KV cache hit rate: 31% for prefixes across top 10 customers; effective saved tokens ~12% at the system level.

Tradeoffs: bigger batching wins on throughput but pushes p95 up — acceptable if we pair with a small regional routing hedge that pins latency-sensitive customers to lower-latency pools.

Attachment: unit_econ_snapshot_v2.pdf (appendix table + charts).

- Rishi: finalized appendix + sensitivity table (reserve 0 / 25 / 50 / 100 GPUs) — deliverable received and attached in the slide deck.
- Karthik: please confirm regional quota checks (eu/us/apac) and whether we can pre-stage 50 GPUs in us-west by Apr 28.

Decision logic included on slide:
1) If expected burst > 2.5x baseline and p95 risk > 10% -> pre-reserve 50 GPUs (3 months) + enable conservative batching (25ms window) + KV cache tuning.
2) If burst < 2.5x -> rely on on-demand + regional routing + model fallback.
